newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens at new record, dollar, Dow boost.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens at new record, dollar, Dow boost.

text.p: The German DAX index surged ahead at the open to reach a new record high on Friday with the market buyoed by a barrage of positive signals.
German stocks took heart from a record close on Wall Street, gains on Japan's Nikkei index, data showing improved German business confidence and a firm dollar, which is positive for German exporters.
The market was also supported by the expiry of certain options contracts on the DAX index of 30 leading shares.
The DAX reached a new bourse high of 2,737.51, up 21.25 points, or 0.78 percent, before slipping back somewhat to trade at 2,734.68.
Dealers said some players had gone short in late floor trading on Thursday on fears over Russian political instability and were hurrying back into the market.
"There could be surprises on the up-side, because the Russian situation isn't as bad as we thought," said one dealer.
The September West German IFO business climate index rose to 95.7 from 94.4, reflecting an improvement in business confidence.
Car maker Daimler Benz continued to be a favourite and traders said the stock could break the 90 mark per share level. Daimler was up 80 pfennigs, or nearly one percent, at 89.25.
Mercedes-Benz, part of the Daimler group, said it had reached record sales for commercial vehicles for the first nine months of 1996.

Sportsware firm Adidas lost the most ground, dropping almost seven percent or 9.80 marks to 133 marks. Dealers said the stock, which had risen after it said it would be a main sponsor of the 1998 soccer World Cup, was not being seen as positively as before by banks.
"There are rumours that earnings downgrades are in the pipeline," said one trader.
New stock dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care added over five percent, rising 6.80 marks to 130.30, after the group's shares gained ground in New York.
